L15: ### 動物の未来を変える、新しいがん治療の開発
L16: 
L17: MESSAGE
L18: ## ごあいさつ
L19: 
L20: どうぶつトランスレーショナルリサーチセンター（略称 iCAT）は、埼玉県所沢市の日本小動物医療センター附属の研究施設です。
L21: 
L22: 動物のがんの克服を目指して、がんについて基礎から臨床までさまざまな角度から研究しています。iCATは、水野拓也と伊賀瀬雅也が運営しており、大学と同等の水準で研究を実施しています。
L23: 
L24: またiCATは、日本小動物がんセンターに併設されているため、がんに関蓮するさまざまな臨床試験や実際の症例組織を用いた解析などを実施しやすい環境が整っております。
L25: 
L26: iCATでは、大学院生として博士号を取得することが可能です。また、臨床現場で働いている獣医師の方々が社会人大学院生として博士号を取得することも支援しています。さらに、関東の獣医系大学からの外部研修生（学部学生・大学院生）に対する研究指導も積極的に行っています。

L20: #  新規抗がん剤による臨床試験(治験)
L21: 
L22: 獣医がん臨床研究グループ(JVCOG)は、新規抗がん剤を用いた犬のがん治療の治験に参加しています。症例をご紹介いただける場合は、最寄りの【12†治験実施施設（下記の施設リストを参照）】へご連絡ください。
L23: 
L24: １．治験の目的
L25:     抗がん剤の効果を腫瘍別に評価し、次期臨床試験の対象腫瘍を選定する。
L26: ２．治験の対象となる動物
L27:     犬
L28: ３．治療の対象となる腫瘍
L29:     ①外科治療困難あるいは再発性肥満細胞腫
L30: ②低分化型リンパ腫
L31: （2016年6月8日より治験対象となる腫瘍種を限定しました）
L32: 
L33: 参加基準の詳細についてはこちら
L34: 
L35: 治験の参加基準について
L36: 
L37: ①組入れ基準
L38:   * (1)病理組織検査にて肥満細胞腫または低分化型リンパ腫と診断され、測定可能な病変*を有する犬。
L39: *肥満細胞腫：10mm以上（X線・エコーでは20mm以上、リンパ節病変は短径15mm以上）
L40: 低分化型リンパ腫：短径15mm以上
L41:   * (2)手術による完全切除が困難と考えられる病変を有する犬。
L42:   * (3)1カ月以上の生存が期待できる犬。
L43:   * (4)病歴及び治療履歴が明らかな犬。
L44: ②除外基準
L45:   * (1)組み入れ判定時の血液学的検査及び血液化学検査で以下のいずれかの基準に該当する場合。
L46: 好中球数 < 2,500/μL、PLT < 100,000/μL、T-BIL > 1.5mg/dL、ALT > 基準値上限の4倍、CRE >基準値上限の1.5倍
L47:   * (2)過去に腫瘍に対して免疫療法、性ホルモン療法を行っている犬。
L48:   * (3)放射線療法を過去に行い、その効果が持続中または不明と判定された犬。
L49:   * (4)被験薬以外の化学療法を過去に行い、その効果が持続中または不明と判定された犬。
L50:   * (5)ステロイド剤および非ステロイド性抗炎症薬（NSAIDs）の全身投与が2週間以内に行われている犬。ただし、これら薬剤を治験開始時に1カ月以上投薬していて、進行性病変を持つ犬は組み入れても良い。
L51:   * (6)妊娠中、授乳中及び妊娠の可能性のある犬、あるいは繁殖を目的とする犬。
L52:   * (7)重篤な骨髄抑制のある犬および感染症が合併している犬。
L53: 
L54: ※治験担当者が本臨床試験に参加可能かどうかを最終的に判断いたしますので、ご了承ください。
L55:

L59: ５．治験薬について
L60:     有効成分は人体用医薬品として承認され、広く使われています。
L61: 海外では動物用として使用されている抗がん剤です。

L63:     治験薬は無償で提供されますが、詳細は治験実施施設までお問い合わせください。

L2: # Immunotherapy
L3: for canine cancer.
L4: 
L5: * * *
L6: 
L7: Intro
L8: 
L9: ### In partnership with Ardent Animal Health, we are developing a dual-action immunotherapy for canine osteosarcoma.
L10: 
L11: ### Osteosarcoma accounts for 85% of bone tumors in dogs and carries a median survival time of less than one year with standard treatment.
L12: ### By applying validated human cancer science, our dual-action immunotherapy is designed to improve outcomes for one of the most common and lethal cancers in dogs.
L13: 
L14: * * *
L15: 
L16: Program
L17: 
L18: Indication: Canine osteosarcoma
L19: 
L20: Mechanism of action: A dual-action immunotherapy combining an autologous vaccine (K9-ACV) with a novel checkpoint inhibitor (CD200AR-L) to stimulate a robust anti-tumor immune response
L21: Origin: The novel checkpoint inhibitor (CD200AR-L) is based on research from the University of Minnesota, with companion animal rights licensed to Unleash Therapeutics, LLC (via OX2 Therapeutics).
L22: 
L23: Partner: 【1†Ardent Animal Health†ardentanimalhealth.com】 - the dual-action immunotherapy combines our novel checkpoint inhibitor with Ardent’s existing autologous cancer vaccine (K9-ACV), and will be commercialized under the Ardent Animal Health brand.
L24: Status: Clinical - we are conducting a multi-center randomized field efficacy study, sponsored by researchers at the University of Illinois College of Veterinary Medicine. Recruitment is now complete.
L25: 
L26: 【2†Learn more about our clinical trial  >>>†studypages.com】
L27: 
L28: * * *
L29: 
L30: About
L31: 
L32: Unleash Therapeutics, LLC is a single-asset company focused exclusively on bringing this immunotherapy to dogs with osteosarcoma.
L33: The company was founded in 2021 by 【3†Dr. Elizabeth Iorns†www.linkedin.com】 and 【4†Dan Knox†www.linkedin.com】. Elizabeth is a cancer biologist whose French Bulldog, Lily, was diagnosed with a terminal brain tumor in 2020. Her experience with Lily's treatment highlighted the gap between human and veterinary oncology — and became the catalyst for Unleash Therapeutics, LLC.
L34: Elizabeth and Dan are also the co-founders of 【5†Familiar†familiartx.com】, an animal health therapeutics company building a broad pipeline of modern medicines for companion animals. They are longtime collaborators who previously co-founded Science Exchange (YC S11), a global R&D marketplace, and who invest together through a shared angel fund across technology and life sciences.

L19: This fully funded, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial will assess a potential new treatment for oral melanoma in dogs.
L20: 
L21: ###### Funding
L22: 
L23: This is a fully funded study.
L24: ###### Owner Participation / Commitment
L25:   * Investigational product or placebo is given once every 2 weeks for approximately 6 months (15 scheduled visits).
L26:   * All study visits must occur at one of the designated clinics listed below.
L27:   * Periodic lab work and thoracic radiographs (x-rays) will be performed to assess each dog’s overall health.
L28:   * Owners are required to sign a consent form before their dog is enrolled, complete owner diaries at home and complete a single quality-of-life assessment question at each visit to the clinic.
L29:   * At study end, dogs are eligible to receive the investigational product in a separate clinical trial.
L30: ###### Eligibility
L31:   * Diagnosis of Stage II or III oral melanoma (not confined to lip)
L32:   * Prior surgery acceptable (if performed at least 14 days prior to enrollment) if measurable disease remains which meets the criteria below
L33:   * If the target lesion was removed, regrowth of the lesion must have a longest diameter of ≥10mm
L34:   * No lung metastasis
L35:   * No prior Oncept^{®} melanoma vaccine
L36:   * Dog must weigh at least 3 kg (6.6 lb)
L37: Other study inclusion and exclusion criteria apply. The Investigator will determine if the dog is a good candidate for this study after examination.

L110: # Current Clinical Trials
L111: We are currently seeking patients for enrollment in funded oncology clinical trials. Study goals and suitability for each patient are discussed in detail with the clients prior to enrollment.
L112: Although clinical trial enrollment may not be the best option for all patients, in many cases, clinical trial participation provides the opportunity to receive novel, cutting-edge therapies free of charge or at a reduced cost and may facilitate treatment of pets where it would not otherwise be possible due to financial constraints or lack of other therapy options. Criteria for enrollment are outlined for each tumor type below.
L113: Please direct referrals or questions to the Oncology Clinical Trials Service at 573-882-7821.
L114: Current Trials and Studies
L115: 
L116: Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor (BI705564) for Canine B‑Cell Lymphoma
L117: 
L118: The University of Missouri Veterinary Health Center is enrolling dogs in a clinical trial evaluating an investigational oral Bruton’s Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) inhibitor—BI705564—for the treatment of newly diagnosed B‑cell lymphoma. This exploratory, multicenter field study aims to assess both efficacy and safety of BTK inhibition in canine patients.
L119: 
L120: Eligibility includes:
L121:   * Dogs >1 year old and 10–50 kg in body weight
L122:   * Naïve, untreated B‑cell lymphoma confirmed by cytology or histology with immunophenotyping (flow cytometry)
